newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks set for pick up in second half 97.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks set for pick up in second half 97.

text.p: Singapore stocks, which turned in a patchy performance in the first half of 1997, should do better for the rest of the year as the island-state's economy picks up, investment analysts say.
Blue-chip stocks have had a dismal first half with the 30-share Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) down about 11 percent from the start of the year. It ended at 1,985.94 points on Friday.
But economists told Reuters last week that the Singapore economy was soon likely to rebound from its recent slowdown, pushing share prices higher.
"I think we will probably see a better performance in the last quarter of the year when the economy would show more strength," said Timothy Wong, research analyst with Vickers Ballas in Singapore.
The key to Singapore's recovery will be the performance of its electronics sector, which accounts for around half its manufacturing output and almost 60 percent of non-oil exports.
A collapse in international demand for electronics products last year hit Singapore badly, but economists say the slump now appears to be coming to an end.
Wong said he expected a "good 20 percent upside" for the STII when recovery comes through, which would place the index at around 2,400.

In terms of valuations, analysts said Singapore looked cheap on a historic basis with the market trading at around 17 times its price earnings (PE) ratio. Historically, Singapore's PE has been within the 16 to 24 times range.
Even if the long-awaited electronics rebound was delayed into the first quarter of 1998, Wong said stocks would probably rise ahead of the rebound as they tended to move three to six months ahead.

High growth stocks listed on the second board, SESDAQ, and electronics stocks have already shown strong gains with the SES Electronics index and UOB-Sesdaq index up 34 percent and 23 percent respectively over the last six months.
But analysts said there needed to be clearer signs of a sustained recovery in the electronics sector before many other industrial sectors saw share price rises.

"In terms of representation in the stock market, electronics is pretty small. But in terms of sentiment and in terms of impact on GDP (gross domestic product) growth, it is tremendous," Tan Min Lan, senior economist and Singapore strategist with Merrill Lynch said.
Tan believes economic fundamentals are mostly in place for a pick up in the second half.
"Cost pressures are low, there is an easier monetary policy and no asset inflation. Also most people expect some tax cuts in the upcoming budget," she said.
Analysts say when a rebound comes about, blue chip banks and property stocks, which have fallen sharply, should benefit because they are traditionally linked to GDP growth.
"The two sectors which would probably do well would be banking, which is seen as a proxy for the economy, and also property, which I think is at the trough of its cycle," said Merrill's Tan.
Among Merrill's picks are OCBC, DBS, First Capital Corp and Keppel Land.

Lee Kin Wah, research manager with Jardine International Securities said the focus would still be on growth stocks and electronic counters in the second half. "But the easy money has been made," he said.
